Azifa Khatun ------Appellant

full_judgment:
Mustafa kamal, J.-- This appeal is directed against the Judgment and order dated 16.1.81 passed by the learned District Judge, Noakhali in Miscellaneous Case No.268 of 1980 under section 263 of the Succession Act, 1925 ( Act XXXIX of 1925). 

 2. The petitioner-appellant filed the said application under Section 263 of the Succession Act, 1925 for revocation of the probate granted to the opposite party-respondent Tulshi Ranjan Roy on 26.7.80 in Miscellaneous Case No. 95 of 1979. The petitioner-appellant stated that she had purchased 1.31 acres of land in 1975 from Nagendra Kumar Roy, the son of the alleged executant of the will. She has possessed the said land. The respondent Tulshi Ranjan Roy obtained the probate by exercising fraud upon the Court She gave details of the alleged fraud in the application. 

 3. The opposite party-respondent filed a written objection and contested the application. He averred that the testator Chandra Kumar Roy died in 1962. He executed the will on 10.7.1961 before his death. The respondent was granted probate in Miscellaneous Case No. 55 of 6179. The application of the petitioner-appellant was not maintainable because she filed an application under Order 1, rule 10 C.P.C. in the said Miscellaneous Case No. 95 of 1979 for being added as a party. Alter hearing both the parties the said application was rejected on 11.6.80. The petitioner appeal last having not challenged the said order of rejection is now debarred from calling into question the grant of probate under section 263 of the Succession Act. 

 5. Mr. Md, Ruhul Amin, the learned Advocate for the petitioner-appellant submits that the petitioner-appellant has every locus standi to apply for revocation of the probate. He cites the case of Sarala Sandari Dassya Vs. Dinabondhu Roy Brajaraf Saha; A.I.R. 1944 (P.C.) 11, in which the Privy Council held that it cannot be said that it is only those persons who could be cited before the grant of probate are the persons who could apply to revoke the probate. If a person complains that he has in fact been defrauded, be is one of the persons who is injured by the fraud alleged and that person is entitled to have his redress by applying to revoke the probate and thereby cause the fraud to become inoperative. As the petitioner appellant has specifically alleged fraud in her application, she is entitled to be heard hi the matter of revocation of the grant of probate, he submits. 

 6. Mr A.Q. Rashid, the learned Advocate for the opposite party-respondent does not challenge the locus natal of the appellant to prefer the application for revocation of the probate. He submits that by accepting the rejection of her own application under Order 1, rule 10 C.P.C. in the previous proceeding for grain of probate, the petitioner-appellant has allowed the same to be concluded without her presence. Now she cannot be concluded to challenge the grant of probate because her conduct will be taken to be acquiescence, He submits several cases in support of his submission. In the case of Namara Nath and another Vs. S. Fakirmani Dassi and others. A.I.R. 1952 (Cal) 20, it has beta held that in case where a person though not served has actual knowledge of the pendency of the proceeding for the grant of probate or Letters of Administration, and has an opportunity to intervene, his knowledge is taken to be a substitute for the legal process of service of notice. In such a case where a person has actual knowledge and has opportunity to intervene and stands by, the person concerned cannot complain of any prejudice and the law, therefore, holds the person bound by the grant of probate or Letters of Administration even though he may not have been served in the course of the proceedings. 

 7. The present case, however, is different from the case just cited by Mr, A.Q. Rashid. The petitioner appellant was not only aware of the previous proceeding for gnat of probate but also applied for being added as a party. Her application was rejected after contest. The present application under section 263 of the Succession Act has been found to be not maintainable, not because she allowed the proceeding to pass by, but because she failed to challenge in the High Court Division the order of rejection. 

 12. In the result the appeal is allowed but without any order as to costs. The Miscellaneous Case is sent back on remand to the probate Court for rehearing on merit on the basis of then existing evidence on record in accordance with law.
